does: Loosens cooked grains with a fork or the fingertips, lifting and separating them, so that the steam escapes and each grain stands apart instead of sitting in a block.
how: Wait until the grains have taken up their liquid and the steam is no longer heavy.
Add a little butter or a trickle of oil, so that the grains stay loose.
Run a fork, or the fingertips, lightly through the grains, lifting from the bottom and letting them fall. Do not press and do not stir.
Rub any lumps between the fingertips to break them.
Cover with a cloth until it is time to serve, so that the grains stay warm without drying.

cues.text: The grains lie loose, each with its own outline, and the heap holds no wet patches.
The fork meets no resistance and the grains fall away from it.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring hard, which breaks the grains and turns them to paste.
mistakes.fix: Lift and let fall, with light strokes.

mistakes.mistake: Fluffing while the grains are still wet, which smears them.
mistakes.fix: Leave them covered until the liquid has gone.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the grains in a heap without airing them, so that they set into a block.
mistakes.fix: Fluff them once more just before serving.

comes_after.why: Couscous is fluffed once it has drunk its liquid, so a cook has to be able to bring the grains to that point first.
Rice is fluffed once it has taken up its water, so a cook has to be able to cook it to that point first.
